analysis.description: This paper explores the theoretical foundations and properties of Generative Flow Networks (GFlowNets), a method for sampling diverse candidates according to a reward function, and compares these methods to Monte-Carlo Markov chains (MCMC). It introduces a new local training objective called detailed balance, explains the concept of conditional GFlowNets, and discusses applications in active learning scenarios.

type.justification: The paper primarily focuses on theoretical aspects of GFlowNets, including properties, training objectives, and comparisons to other models.
type.quote: In this paper, we show a number of additional theoretical properties of GFlowNets, including a new local and efficient training objective called detailed balance for the analogy with MCMC.

name.justification: The paper suggests using GFlowNets to train energy-based models by sampling configurations proportionally to an energy function.

name.quote: GFlowNets amortize the work typically done by computationally expensive MCMC methods in a single but trained generative pass.
